records.subagent_summary: Execution 148.75 scored 3 of 8. Three failures ran into the 16384-token cap with no boxed answer at all; the two that stopped declared every branch contradictory and then named an arbitrary candidate. The recurring logical error is treating "cannot determine" as a claim to refute rather than a survivor count over cases the speakers themselves cannot distinguish. Rounds 1-3 all attacked this with longer, more puzzle-specific wording (150/167/102 tokens) and each lost held-out accuracy against the 77-token incumbent, so this edit stays terse and deliberately generic: name what the data leaves open, enumerate cases as a list, read knowledge claims as counts, recheck the survivor against all conditions, stop when reasoning repeats, and always emit one boxed answer. The verify, anti-loop and commit clauses help ordinary problems too, so it should transfer instead of over-fitting.

Fresh rollouts (execution_id 148.76) scored 7/8, the incumbent's first train miss in four rounds: the failed trace derived the correct locus quadratic early, then spent over 30k characters insisting the unnormalized A(x^2+y^2)+Bx+D form was an ellipse and that |z| should be constant, looping through recomputed sample roots until it hit the length cap with no boxed answer. Six of the seven passing traces also paid for that same doubt before normalizing. Round 2 showed a bare normalize-and-non-origin warning only ties held-out, so this edit instead supplies the missing certification (equal square coefficients and no xy term mean circle regardless of scale or center) that terminates the stall, then keeps the divide-by-A, complete-the-square, and box-the-answer steps.

Fresh round-4 rollouts under the 147-token incumbent scored 1/8. Reward requires a boxed value after the reasoning block closes: four of eight never closed it, and two closed it then began a long fresh write-up and were cut off mid-derivation, despite having already boxed the correct value inside the reasoning. Six of eight held the correct exact value by 7-16 percent of the trace, so the loss is the output protocol, not the method; the incumbent's shoelace/invariance recipe was executed essentially never (0-1 mentions). Rounds 2-3 showed extra prohibitions and a generic case-scoring rule both lose, so this revision names the grading gate, caps reasoning at the halfway mark, forbids re-deriving in the write-up, and compresses the geometry to one reusable wedge fact at 122 tokens versus 147.

Fresh round-4 rollouts (execution 148.78) scored 2/8 with the incumbent. All six failures report one factor instead of the total, from two root causes: a belief that handing off between polynomials breaks the progression at block boundaries, which makes them discard the product they had already written and fall back to the per-polynomial cap (the two rollouts that hit the token ceiling spent their whole tail on that false contradiction), and an off-by-one in the cap in both directions, once as degree-minus-one and once as degree-plus-one interpolation points. The revision is shorter than the incumbent (150 vs 153 tokens): it drops the redundant grouping clause, pins the cap as exactly deg P in both directions, and states that all blocks lie on the same affine target so concatenation cannot break the spacing.

Seven of eight rollouts were correct; the lone failure never subtracted the two curve equations, folded the constant output difference into the logarithm term by term, produced an irrational discriminant, and burned all 16384 tokens with no boxed value. Every success ran one identical chain: pin parameters and verify, translate the vector relation into coordinates, subtract the two curve equations so a single exponentiation clears the logs, factor the resulting quadratic, drop the root reproducing a given point, then shoelace over all four vertices in cyclic order. My discarded rounds 2 and 3 replaced that last step with a cross product at one vertex, which no success uses, and both lost training accuracy while gaining held-out. This revision keeps the transferable subtraction move and restores the shoelace finish the successes rely on, at incumbent length.

records.mutation: uncovering-first: chosen item must be uncovered, so the event is a multi-move run to write out and price, not one coin flip
records.subagent_summary: All 8 fresh rollouts scored 0, and every one mis-priced part (b): six treated "a chosen item arrives at the destination first" as a single coin flip or a symmetry claim and answered 1/2, 1/4 or 1/k, while two declared it outright impossible. None noticed that the item must first be uncovered, i.e. that the items above it have to be relayed out of the way, so the event is a multi-move run rather than one choice. The incumbent already supplies bottom-equals-arrived-first and the forced-move weight, so this edit adds the missing uncovering step and requires the run to be written out and priced move by move, a general habit for any relay/shunting process rather than a fact about one problem.

Fresh round-4 rollouts under the incumbent scored 1/8. The only winner was also the only rollout that reached three exact small cases and tabulated the requested value before generalizing; every zero either stopped after two cases or delayed the shrink until deep into the trace after long symbolic work at full size, and four hit the generation cap. The incumbent's ban on the single-polynomial model is now partly obeyed, but students substitute an equally fatal habit: manipulating the huge parameter symbolically. This edit makes the shrink the literal first action, sets a concrete quota of three tabulated entries before generalizing, and extends the ban to full-size symbolic work, going 78 to 73 tokens since shorter has won every kept round.

Fresh round-4 rollouts on the incumbent scored 5/8, and all three failures shared one mechanism: they divided the stage totals by a grouping count stated in the text and justified it as the more realistic figure; two had already derived the full common-divisor list and abandoned it, one skipped divisibility outright. The incumbent's grouping-count sentence is abstract bookkeeping and demonstrably does not stop this, so I swapped it for a reusable elimination discipline: a candidate may only be discarded by a stated condition, never by apparent plausibility. Round 3 taught me that patching this failure with an added tiebreak rule saturates train but destroys transfer, while compressing and deleting wins; this revision adds no rule and lands at 133 tokens versus 136.

Fresh training on the incumbent scored 4/8 and all four failures ran to the 16384-token cap. Two derived the reflection constant by averaging the inputs they were asked to evaluate instead of from the given data, one abandoned the symmetry for multinomial coefficient matching, and one actually reached the correct values through a fixed-point equation but then burned the rest of its budget re-expanding the composition numerically and never committed an answer. The edit keeps the involution ansatz that earns the current score and adds the two general moves the failures lacked: plug a requested input into the identity itself, which typically reduces to a solvable fixed-point equation in one unknown, and stop after one small symmetry check rather than re-verifying the composition.

Fresh round-4 rollouts under the incumbent scored 4/8. All three cap-exhausted failures abandoned their literal run partway and looped inside symbolic transposition and cycle bookkeeping, re-deriving jargon instead of counting; the one finished failure declared the stages disjoint transpositions and read the period off a single stage. Every success instead re-applied the entire operation repeatedly on the two smallest sizes, counted applications until the state returned, and fit the parameter. The incumbent's 'describe it as a single map and check the two agree' clause is what invites that fatal symbolic detour, so I replace it with an explicit count-applications-until-return loop plus a ban on position algebra, holding length at 108 tokens because my two long caution-list proposals both cut held-out.
